Oblivionフォント(.fnt)のグリフレコード対応は record = ASCII - 1。レコード0-31は空、レコード32=! (ASCII 33)。text_renderer.cppのloadOblivionFont()で glyphs[i+1] に格納。スペース(ASCII 32)は合成グリフ(advance=fontSize*0.35)。
OblivionフォントテクスチャはRGBA8でグリフデータはアルファチャンネル。フラグメントシェーダーの useAlphaChannel=1 で .a をサンプリング。RobotoはGL_R8で useAlphaChannel=0 (.r)。

Oblivion ESM/ESP binary format confirmed: 20-byte record header (NOT the 16-byte header used by Skyrim/Fallout). Record = tag(4) + dataSize(4) + flags(4) + formID(4) + version(2) + unknown(2) = 20 bytes. GRUP = 'GRUP'(4) + size(4) + label(4) + groupType(4) + skip(4) = 20 bytes. Subrecord = tag(4) + size(2) = 6 bytes, with size masked by (size & 0xFFFF). TES4 header record sits at offset 0 with dataSize=744, flags=1, formID=0, so the first GRUP is at offset 764 (20 + 744). app/src/main/cpp/assets/esm_reader.cpp already implements this format correctly (L116 'TES4 record: 20-byte header', L183 'remaining 16 bytes', L86 'GRUP header (20 bytes)', L471 size & 0xFFFF + offset += 6). CRITICAL: records with size 0 are LEGAL and are NOT terminators; treating them as errors truncates the scan.

CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (this entry previously blamed text_renderer.cpp). The 1-2 FPS reading was a degraded-emulator symptom, not an app bug: the emulator had run out of RAM and was swapping (TOTAL SWAP PSS 223 MB). With NO app change, restarting the emulator (adb emu kill -> emulator.exe -avd Pixel_API34 -no-snapshot-load) gives 30-33 FPS in gameplay and 60 FPS at the title screen (EGL app_time_stats avg=31.11/32.32/33.69/34.11 ms), and ESM parse time fell from 222 s to 13 s. Reducing native heap is the Phase 65/66 item; text_renderer batching is not the cause.

Oblivion Script VM instruction format (confirmed from script_vm.cpp and script_disasm.cpp): each instruction is opcode(uint16 LE) + argLength(uint16 LE) + argData(argLength), i.e. a 4-byte header. argLength==0 instructions (ADD/POP/NEG/CMP) still consume 4 bytes. STOP must be 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00. Opcode values: STOP=0x0000, ADD=0x0001, NEG=0x0006, JUMP=0x0010, JUMP_Z=0x0011, PUSH_INT=0x0012, PUSH_FLOAT=0x0013, PUSH_REF=0x0015, POP=0x0016, DUP=0x0017, GET_LOCAL=0x0020, GET_GLOBAL=0x0022, CALL=0x1000. JUMP/JUMP_Z targets are ABSOLUTE program counters (ctx.setPC(target)), not relative offsets. execute(ctx, maxInstructions) returns VMResult::FrameBudget when the budget is exhausted.

app/src/main/cpp/include/glm/glm.hpp is a hand-written minimal GLM stub, NOT real GLM. vec3 exposes only vec3(), vec3(x,y,z), public x/y/z, operator+ - * /, dot, cross, length, normalize. There is NO operator[] and NO single-float constructor, so 'v[i]' and 'glm::vec3(0.0f)' fail to compile. Use explicit component math or copy into a float array, and always pass three floats to the constructor. Free functions glm::dot / glm::cross / glm::length / glm::normalize do exist.

QuestManager semantics (deliberate, do not 'fix'): updateObjectiveProgress() auto-completes a quest as soon as allObjectivesCompleted() is true, by calling checkAndCompleteQuest() -> completeQuest(). completeQuest() is NOT idempotent - it returns false and logs a warning if the quest is already COMPLETED (failQuest() is symmetric). Auto-completion is called from both updateObjectiveProgress() and update(). QuestStageManager::checkCompletionStage() forwards completeQuest()'s bool, but its only call site (quest_stage_manager.cpp:350) discards it, so the non-idempotent result causes no production harm.

CharacterStatus::initialize(baseHealth, baseMana, level) no longer applies level scaling; it sets maxHealth = baseHealth, maxMana = baseMana, and now also stores this->level = level. Rationale: every other assignment site (npc_manager.cpp:213,334, ui_character_creation.cpp:35,37, both Phase45 tests) set raw values, and the only production caller passes level=1, so the old formula (base * (1 + level*0.1)) was a constant 1.1x inflation rather than scaling. Effect: GameState player 110/132 -> 100/120; NPC 110/55 -> 100/50. attributes/skills still receive level-based additions; revisit in Phase64.

CollisionWorld::getBodyCount() now returns the new liveBodyCount_ member instead of bodies.size(). bodies is a slot array: addBody() reuses freeSlots or push_backs, and removeBody() only sets id=-1, isActive=false and push_backs the slot, so the vector never shrinks. removeBody() also gained a double-free guard (if bodies[bodyId].id == NULL_BODY return;). getBodyCount() has no production consumers - only Phase30 tests - so the capacity->live-count change is behaviour-neutral outside tests.

Save-system design gap (not a one-line bug): the save system proxies mana with stamina because Player (game/player.h) has maxHealth/maxMagicka/maxStamina but NO current-magicka field. save_system/save_manager.cpp binary path writes player->stamina / player->maxStamina (L60-61) and reads them back (L286-287); the GameState path maps playerStatus.currentMana = player->stamina and maxMana = player->maxStamina (L685-686). Consequently maxMagicka is NEVER persisted. Changing only L686 to maxMagicka would mix two attributes into one stat, so decide first whether Player gets a real magicka pool. Deferred to Phase69 (persistence).

Oblivion MGEF/SPEL/ENCH/INGR/ALCH binary layout (empirically confirmed with Python probes mgef_probe7..12 against the real Oblivion.esm). MGEF subrecord is DATA (36 or 64 bytes; NOT MEDT): off4=baseCost(float), off8=actorValue(uint32), off12=school(0-5), off16=flags. SPEL subrecord SPIT is 16 bytes: off0=spellType, off4=cost, off8=level, off12=uninitialized (0xCDCDCD00; NOT flags). EFID (4 bytes) is the MGEF editorID ASCII code (e.g. FIDG, RESP, INVI), NOT a formID. EFIT is 24 bytes: off0-3 = EFID echo, off4=magnitude, off8=area, off12=duration, off16=unused, off20=actorValue. The old code read magnitude/area/duration from off0/off4/off8, i.e. 4 bytes off; that was the direct cause of 0 spells being assigned. INGR/ALCH: DATA is only 4 bytes (float weight) and ENIT is 8 bytes (off0=value, off4=flags).

Oblivion EFIT magnitude is stored as EITHER int32 OR float depending on the record (proven by mgef_probe11: int values appear as denormal floats such as 1.4e-45). Read it with the helper readFloatOrInt() in assets/esm_reader.cpp: if the float is 0, non-finite, |f|<1e-6, or |f|>1e9, reinterpret the 4 bytes as int32. Distribution of raw off4 values across 1137 SPEL EFITs: 0(334), 100(226), 10(214), 20(169), 5(136), 50(119), 30(87), 15(84), 25(82), 1(41).

Oblivion MGEF actorValue (DATA off8) full semantics, confirmed for all 145 MGEFs (mgef_probe12). 0 = special/generic effect (LOCK, OPEN, DISPL, TELE, REAN, TURN, VAMP, DIAR, DIWE, DRSK, SUDG, POSN, COCR, COHU, LGHT, ABAT, ABSK, CUxx, FOAT, FOSK, REAT, STRP, SEFF). 8 = Health (ABHE, DGHE, DRHE, FIDG, FOHE, FRDG, REHE, SHDG). 9 = Magicka (ABSP, DGSP, DRSP, FOSP, RESP; 'SP' = spell points = Magicka, so Restore Magicka is RESP, not RSPA). 10 = Fatigue (ABFA, DGFA, DRFA, FOFA, REFA). 11 = Speed (BRDN, FTHR). 33-70 = skills/attributes (CALM=33, DEMO=34, FOMM=40, NEYE=41, SHLD=43, CHML=46, INVI=47, PARA=48, SLNC=49, SABS=52, RFLC=53, WABR=55, WAWA=56, STMA=57, DTCT=58, REDG=59, TELE=60, FISH/RSFI/WKFI=61, FRSH/RSFR/WKFR=62, RSDI/WKDI=63, RSMA/WKMA=64, RSNW/WKNW=65, RSPA=66, RSPO/WKPO=67, LISH/RSSH/WKSH=68, DARK=70). >100 = formID link; ALL 62 Conjuration MGEFs are formID links (Bound Weapons BW01-BW08, Summons Z001-Z019, Bound Armor BABO-BASH, MYTH/MYHL). Use a threshold of 200 to split actorValue from linkedFormID.

Oblivion SPEL records do NOT store a magic school; it must be derived from the spell's magic effects. Because EFID holds an editorID code rather than a formID, references cannot be resolved during the single decode pass. Implemented a two-phase scheme: ESMFile::resolveMagicReferences() runs after all records are decoded and maps effectCodes -> effectFormIDs and derives spell.school from the first effect's MGEF school. ESMManager::rebuildIndices() runs a SECOND pass that builds a global editorID->MGEF map across all loaded files and re-resolves each file, so DLC plugin spells link to master (Oblivion.esm) MGEFs. MagicEffectData pointers in ESMManager::m_magicEffectByEditorID are only valid after rebuildIndices() (it clears them on every rebuild).

game/spell_manager.cpp mgefToEffectType() now takes const oblivion::MagicEffectData* instead of a formID. The old hardcoded formID switch (0x0001E825 etc.) was entirely wrong: real MGEF formIDs are 0x00001881-style, so every effect fell back to DAMAGE. Classification now keys off the MGEF editorID code plus school/linkedFormID: FIDG/FRDG/SHDG/DG*/DR*/WK*/AB* -> DAMAGE, REHE/FOHE/CU* -> HEAL, RESP/FOSP/FOMM -> RESTORE_MANA, REFA/FOFA -> RESTORE_STAMINA, PARA -> PARALYZE, INVI -> INVISIBILITY, school==1 && linkedFormID!=0 -> SUMMON, fallback = DAMAGE when school==2 else FORTIFY_ATTR.

SELinux MLS pitfall on the Android emulator: files placed with adb push get u:object_r:app_data_file:s0:c192,... while the app itself runs as s0:c193,... and SELinux denies the read. After every adb push of game data you MUST run: adb shell chcon -R u:object_r:app_data_file:s0:c193,c256,c512,c768 /data/data/com.example.oblivion/files/data

Confirmed ESM subrecord layouts for the secondary record types. PGRD: PGRP is a 16-byte stride (x,y,z float + unused uint32), PGAG is 1 bit per point (bytes = ceil(N/8)), PGRR is 4-byte stride, PGRL is 12 raw bytes; PGRD has no own cell formID, it must use the GRUP parent cell formID. PGRD is always a compressed record (flags bit18) and the reader decompresses it before decoding. GMST: EDID + DATA whose type is derived from the first EDID character (s=string, f=float, i=int, b=bool). GLOB: EDID + FNAM(1, type char) + FLTV(4, float). LTEX: EDID + ICON + HNAM(3, rgb) + SNAM(1). DOOR: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + SCRI(4) + SNAM(4) + ANAM(4) + FNAM(1 flags). GRAS: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + DATA(32) where DATA offset 2 is maxSlope. FURN: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + MNAM(4). AMMO: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + ENAM(4) + DATA(18). SLGM: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + SCRI(4) + DATA(8) + SOUL(1, current soul) + SLCP(1, capacity). KEYM: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + DATA(8). SBSP: EDID + DNAM(12, 3 floats). SGST: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + MODT(96) + ICON + repeated EFID(4)+EFIT(24) + DATA(9). WTHR: EDID + CNAM + DNAM + NAM0(160) + FNAM(16) + HNAM(56) + DATA(15) + SNAM(8)*N. IDLE: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + CTDA(24)*N + ANAM(1) + DATA(8). CSTY: EDID + CSTD(124) whose first 2 bytes are a uint16 (weaponFlags) followed by floats. LSCR: EDID + ICON + DESC + LNAM(12) whose first 4 bytes are a formID. ANIO: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + DATA(4, formID). WATR: EDID + TNAM + ANAM(1) + FNAM(1) + MNAM(1) + SNAM(4) + DATA(102, floats) + GNAM(12). EFSH: EDID + ICON(1) + ICO2 + DATA(224) whose first int32s are flag groups.

ESM pitfall: LAND, PGRD, REFR, ACHR and ACRE records do not carry their own cell formID. The owning cell must be recovered by tracking the label of the enclosing GRUP with groupType == 6 (CellChildren). Two code paths need this: the file parse path uses a groupInfoStack and the memory parse path uses m_currentCellFormID. Oblivion GRUP types: 0=TopLevel, 1=WorldChildren, 2=InteriorCellBlock, 3=InteriorCellSubBlock, 4=ExteriorCellBlock, 5=ExteriorCellSubBlock, 6=CellChildren, 7=TopicChildren, 8=CellPersistentChildren, 9=CellTemporaryChildren. Also note SubRecord has no empty() member; use size() > 0.

Mandatory rules before trusting any emulator FPS or timing number (established 2026-09-22 after the 1-2 FPS misdiagnosis): (1) Always restart the emulator first - adb emu kill, wait for qemu-system-x86_64.exe to disappear, then emulator.exe -avd Pixel_API34 -no-snapshot-load. (2) Check TOTAL SWAP PSS before measuring: adb shell dumpsys meminfo com.example.oblivion | Select-String "TOTAL PSS|SwapPss"; a value like 223 MB makes the measurement worthless. (3) Re-issue adb root - it is lost on emulator restart, and without it am start fails with "java.lang.SecurityException: Permission Denial: starting Intent ... from null (uid=2000) not exported from uid 10193" because MainActivity is exported=false; NO app log appears at all, which is easily mistaken for the app failing to start. (4) Run adb logcat -c before polling - logcat -d returns the whole buffer, so stale lines get re-matched and produce bogus elapsed times (e.g. "PARSED at 556s" when the parse actually took 13 s).

The emulator's GL transport cannot be switched from pipe to address_space on this host (verified 2026-09-22). "-prop ro.boot.qemu.gltransport.name=address_space" is silently ignored (getprop still reports pipe; ro.boot.* is populated from the kernel command line, not by -prop), and "-feature GLDirectMem" has no effect either. The guest does expose /dev/goldfish_address_space plus the goldfish_address_space module, so only the host side is disabled. advancedFeatures.ini in Sdk\emulator\lib has GLDirectMem = off, GLAsyncSwap = on, GLESDynamicVersion = off, Vulkan = off, GLDMA/GLDMA2 = on. Not a practical problem: a fresh emulator reaches 30-33 FPS over the pipe transport.

Native heap is the binding performance constraint on the emulator (measured 2026-09-22): Native Heap 641,065 KB (626 MB) and TOTAL PSS 685,640 KB (670 MB) with 25 files / 3,109.5 MB of real game data loaded (35,494 cells, 1,029,280 refs, 31,823 terrains, 2,482 NPCs). The 2 GB AVD has no headroom, which is what causes the swapping. The ESM reader does NOT keep a whole-file buffer - assets/esm_reader.cpp streams with std::ifstream + seekg - so the cost is the retained record model: ESMRecord holds std::vector<SubRecord> subRecords and every SubRecord holds std::vector<uint8_t> data, i.e. the raw subrecord payloads of all ~1.17 M records stay resident. Reducing this (decode into typed structs and drop raw payloads, or release subrecords for record types that are fully decoded) is the highest-value Phase 65/66 work item.

Build/install pitfalls confirmed on this project: piping gradlew output directly into Select-String corrupts the produced APK (install then fails with INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_NOT_APK) - always redirect with Out-File and Select-String the file afterwards. Never use "am kill-all": it takes down system_server and reboots Android. app/build.gradle must keep abiFilters 'arm64-v8a', 'armeabi-v7a', 'x86_64' so the emulator runs native x86_64 instead of under ARM-to-x86 binary translation (which caused input-dispatch ANRs); verify with dumpsys package com.example.oblivion | Select-String primaryCpuAbi. A clean assembleDebug for all 3 ABIs takes about 6 min 12 s and produces an 85.5 MB APK.

ROOT CAUSE of the gameplay frame-rate ceiling, confirmed by measurement: ui/ui_draw_helper.cpp called glGetUniformLocation on EVERY draw call (2 per drawColoredQuad, 3 per drawTexturedQuad, 5 per drawGradientQuad, 7 per drawRadialGlow, 16 per draw3DTextureQuad). Each call is a synchronous round-trip to the GL server, so the in-game HUD issued hundreds per frame. Evidence chain: PerformanceMonitor reported a Min Frame Time floor of 37.19 ms (27 fps best case); pointing the camera at empty sky did not change the frame rate (so it was not fragment load); the title screen ran at 60 fps because it draws no HUD; simpleperf attributed 83.22% of samples to goldfish_pipe.ko:goldfish_pipe_read_write with under 0.1% in app code; top -H showed the GL thread at 96.5% and every other thread at 0.0%. FIX: memoize locations per (program, name) in an unordered_map keyed by program id, cleared in UIDrawHelper::cleanup(). RESULT: in-game 19.3 -> 42.7 fps, Average Frame Time 57.78 -> 22.06 ms, Min Frame Time 37.19 -> 15.63 ms, title unchanged at 60. engine/shader.cpp and ui/text_renderer.cpp already cached their locations, which is why the 3D mesh paths were never the bottleneck. LESSON: on this emulator any GL call that needs a server round-trip inside a per-frame loop is a frame-rate cliff - cache every location and never query GL state per draw.

TerrainData reworked to cut native heap and to fix a silent terrain bug. New layout: std::vector<int8_t> heightDeltas (1089 raw VHGT bytes) + float heightOffset + baseTextures[4] + textureFormIDs, with expandHeights()/heightAt() helpers and GRID = 33. Consumers updated: engine/renderer.cpp, world/landscape_renderer.cpp (expands once locally and reuses for 4 quadrants), assets/world_data_loader.cpp. Measured: native heap allocation 704,684 KB -> 430,916 KB; Native Heap SwapPss 629,158 -> 33,981 KB (-95%); TOTAL SWAP PSS 648,001 -> 49,735 KB (-92%). THE BUG THIS FIXED: the old decoder required the Morrowind 65x65 int16 VHGT (size() >= 8451) while TES4's VHGT is 1096 bytes, so hasHeights() was ALWAYS false and every terrain silently rendered as a flat plane. Expansion formula validated independently in Python against Oblivion.esm: (heightOffset + columnOffset + rowOffset) * 8.0f, 14,052/14,613 east-edge and 14,066/14,608 north-edge heights agree (96%; the rest are cells from different worldspaces sharing grid coords). VNML/VCLR parsing was deleted - calculateNormals() derives normals from heights and VCLR was unused.

Known remaining memory item, NOT yet fixed. engine/renderer.cpp assigns cell->heightData = terrain.expandHeights() inside the loop over all 31,823 terrain records, so all 14,686 matched exterior cells each hold 1089 floats (4356 B) = about 64 MB, although only the 9 active cells are ever rendered. Deliberately left alone because Cell::getTerrainHeightAt() reads heightData from other systems and returning 0 for an unloaded cell would change object placement and player grounding. Fixing it needs a compact or lazily expanded representation plus an audit of those callers. Note the current behaviour is MORE correct than before: the flat-terrain fallback meant only the 9 loaded cells had heights at all. plan.md previously claimed '9 active cells only, about 39 KB', which never matched the implementation and has been corrected.
